evidence.estrutura: Ardern governed New Zealand’s unitary parliamentary state with strong national crisis coordination; this supports coordinated central capacity within democracy.
evidence.representacao: Her parliamentary and prime-ministerial career operated through competitive elections and accountable democratic institutions.
evidence.poder: Her government combined rights-based democracy with strong public-health restrictions, firearms regulation and online-harm/security responses; moderate-to-high regulatory state power rather than libertarian minimalism.
evidence.imigracao: Her governments defended multicultural inclusion and refugee commitments while maintaining ordinary border controls; relatively pluralist but regulated.
evidence.diplomacia: She emphasized multilateralism, international cooperation and negotiated responses, supporting a diplomatic orientation.
evidence.intervencao: New Zealand remained an allied security partner but her public style emphasized international law and multilateral cooperation rather than unilateral force.
evidence.economia: Her Labour governments combined private markets with welfare expansion, child-poverty policy and public investment; center-left mixed economy.
evidence.controle: Public-health, labor, housing and welfare policies support substantial regulation without command planning.
evidence.comercio: New Zealand remained strongly integrated into global trade and supported trade agreements; relatively open commerce.
evidence.religiao: Ardern left the Mormon church and governed in secular terms; strongly secular public politics.
evidence.moral: Social inclusion, reproductive-rights reform and equality policies place her on the progressive side.
evidence.tecnologia: Her government engaged digital harms, online extremism and modern public-service technology, favoring regulated pragmatic technology.
